highlights.1.title: Main vs Satellite Campuses
highlights.1.desc: UTM/UTSC and UBC Okanagan admission scores 10-15% lower — a great pathway into top universities
highlights.2.title: Math ~9pts easier than CS
highlights.2.desc: Math admission typically 9-10pts lower than CS at same university, e.g. McMaster Math 85% vs CS 94%
highlights.3.title: Tuition gap up to ¥1M
highlights.3.desc: Memorial ¥60-90K/yr vs UTSG ¥210-340K/yr — 4-year difference up to ¥1M

highlights.4.desc: Dual enrollment at 18/26 schools, minimum IELTS 4.0 accepted for pathway programs
highlights.5.title: 20+ universities have Co-op
highlights.5.desc: Most offer Co-op in Engineering/CS — gain work experience while earning tuition
highlights.6.title: Australia Foundation from IELTS 5.0
highlights.6.desc: UNSW & QS Top 50 foundation programs accept IELTS 5.0, 91% progression rate
highlights.7.title: Satellite campus 'score discount'
highlights.7.desc: UTM CS mid-high 80s vs UTSG ~93% — same degree, 10-15% easier entry
highlights.8.title: 15pt difference within same school
highlights.8.desc: Psychology 10-15pts lower than CS at same school — choosing the right major matters
highlights.9.title: Ranking ≠ Admission Difficulty
highlights.9.desc: Some QS Top 100 universities admit at 75-80% for certain programs
highlights.10.title: Early application advantage
highlights.10.desc: Popular programs close Jan 15; early rolling admission locks in seats
highlights.11.title: 75%+ of resources in ON/BC
highlights.11.desc: Toronto/Vancouver offer most internships and jobs among tracked universities
highlights.12.title: 'Niche' programs at elite schools
highlights.12.desc: UofT/McMaster admit at 80-85% for some programs vs 95%+ for CS/Engineering

insights.finding1.title: UofT satellite campuses much easier than main campus
insights.finding1.desc: UTM CS requires mid-high 80s, your GPA 89.6 already exceeds (vs UTSG 93% competitive average / 97.2% median admission, 3.4pt gap); UTSC Psychology only needs mid-high 70s, you're well above, and it has Co-op. This is the biggest 'hidden gem' opportunity.
insights.finding2.title: UBC Okanagan 10pts lower than Vancouver, with dual admission
insights.finding2.desc: UBC Okanagan Engineering 80-85% fully qualifies you, with EFP English pathway dual admission. Compared to UBC Vancouver Engineering 92%+ admission line, Okanagan is a great gateway into the UBC system.
insights.finding3.title: Math ~9pts easier than CS
insights.finding3.desc: McMaster Math 85% vs CS 94%, you're right at the Math line. If interested in Math, it can be a stepping stone to minor in or transfer to CS.
insights.finding4.title: Psychology 10-15pts easier than CS
insights.finding4.desc: Alberta Psychology 75% vs CS 82%, your 89.6 is well above Psychology line. Consider youth Psychology — UofT UTSC has Co-op and friendly admission.
insights.finding5.title: TMU (formerly Ryerson) CS 82% — fully qualified
insights.finding5.desc: Downtown Toronto + Co-op + IELTS 5.0 dual admission met — one of the most realistic options among city universities.
insights.finding6.title: U of Ottawa IELTS 4.0+ for dual admission
insights.finding6.desc: Your IELTS 5.0 exceeds EIP dual threshold (4.0+), Engineering/CS/Math/Psychology all available for dual admission. Ottawa is the capital, strong Co-op, good overall ranking (QS 2027 #228).
insights.finding7.title: UofT UTSC/UTM no dual admission, main campus IFP has per-band threshold
insights.finding7.desc: UTSC and UTM require IELTS 6.5(6.0) direct admission, no pathway/dual channels. UTSG has IFP but 2026-27 new threshold requires per-band ≥5.0, with multiple IFP streams (Applied Science&Engineering/Arts&Science/Architecture/Landscape Design/Music). CS can use Arts&Science IFP.
insights.finding8.title: Dual admission has program restrictions
insights.finding8.desc: UofT IFP covers Arts&Science/Architecture/Music but new per-band threshold ≥5.0; York Engineering requires IELTS 7.5 and doesn't accept dual; Alberta EAP excludes Engineering. Always verify if your target program is covered by dual admission.
insights.finding9.title: Tuition gap is massive
insights.finding9.desc: Memorial only ¥60-90K/year, UofT UTSG up to ¥210-340K/year — 4-year difference of ¥600K-1M.
insights.finding10.title: Australia foundation is your safety net
insights.finding10.desc: UNSW Extended Foundation IELTS 5.0(4.5) threshold met. 15-month foundation + 91% progression rate, QS #19.
insights.stratA.title: Plan A: Safe & Steady (Start Now)
insights.stratA.item1: U of Ottawa (dual threshold 4.0+, you're at 5.0)
insights.stratB.title: Plan B: Stretch & Optimize (Need IELTS 6.5)
insights.stratB.item2: UofT UTSC Psychology (mid-high 70s, well above + Co-op)
insights.stratB.item3: UBC Okanagan Engineering (80-85%, fully qualified + EFP dual)
insights.stratC.title: Plan C: Australia Foundation (Safety Net)
insights.stratC.item5: Seamless switch to Australia if Canada doesn't work out
insights.tl1.title: Complete safety school applications
insights.tl1.desc: Ottawa, Windsor, Manitoba, Memorial, Concordia — these schools have rolling admissions or late deadlines, but apply early for early offers

insights.tl2.desc: Reading 4.5→6.0 and Listening 4.5→6.0 are your biggest gaps. Recommend 2hrs/day intensive listening + reading with practice tests.
